migration.notes:
51 of 51 coverage entries replayed clean (references, labels, move-result, branch offsets, register moves, register flow, return types); the battery toggle row is withheld, see migration/coverage-exclusions.json. The custom hunks are gated by migration/hunk-contracts.json plus scripts/verify_214_custom_hunks.py, which re-derives every entry from the 194 delta (instruction shape and frame growth, payload literals, the reviewed splice recomputed from the 214 upstream, the register/encoding law, the contracts, the custom-only surfaces, and the type each register provably holds where a hunk reads it) and is enforced by scripts/migrate_214.py; scripts/selftest_214_hunk_gate.py corrupts one reviewed property at a time to prove the gate goes red. The type walk is also run over the pristine 214 tree (--type-flow-control), which reports nothing; it is what the first 214 build failed on (VerifyError in hi1.d), and scripts/port_214_candidate.py now mirrors a customization's register rename onto the line the port keeps, recorded per line in migration/port-report.json. A second device crash came from the other direction: a `replace` hunk carried the register numbering of the frame it was written in (`Ljk5;->c` handed the `Ljava/lang/String;` slot v14 to `Lcom/box/app/vpn/VpnBridge;->key(Lbr5;)I` because 194 kept that enum in v14 and 214 moved it to v15), so scripts/port_214_candidate.py now also re-spells a replaced line's operands from the two versions of the line it replaces (1 line, recorded in migration/port-report.json under registerRealignments), and the type-flow gate was widened from "uncast Object in a narrowed slot" to any mismatch it can prove from this tree's class hierarchy - with the pristine 214 tree still reporting nothing. A third device crash was not a verifier rejection at all: `Resources$NotFoundException: String resource ID #0x0` from the core-detail row, because the reviewed placement for `Lpa1;->a(` kept 194's `const/4 v15, 0x0` flag clear while 214 reads the string resource id in v15 and the flag in v4 - the arm zeroed the id it had just computed. The pin lost that line (its `evidence` now names all three register roles) and scripts/verify_214_custom_hunks.py gained an eighth gate, check_grafted_arm_roles, which re-derives every anchor+insert placement and reports a value the arm takes from an invoke being re-written before the jump onto a merge that still reads it; scripts/selftest_214_hunk_gate.py corrupts that line back in to prove it (13 rows). Integers, so no type walk and no name-based check can see it - which is why the gate now also checks the reviewed placements against themselves. A fourth device crash came from the same arm one step further: `NullPointerException ... Object.getClass() on a null object reference` at `v74.d` called from `ba1.c:573`, because 214 reuses the flag register for something live - every stock arm that reaches `:goto_6` does `move-object/from16 v22, v4` before `const/4 v4, 0x0`, since the merge hands `v22` to `Lv74;->d(...)` as its `Lyw1;` argument - while 194 zeroed an idle register and carried no spill, so the reviewed placement had to gain that move (7 lines to 8) and the ported method is again byte-identical to the 214 upstream except for those 8 lines. scripts/verify_214_custom_hunks.py gained a ninth gate, check_grafted_arm_spills, the mirror of the eighth: it reads the reviewed `insert` (located by its `anchor`) rather than the tree, collects every arm of the ported file that jumps to the same label, and only when saving-before-reusing is that release's habit for all of them does it require the grafted arm to do the same - so a pin that omits a line cannot silence the check by omitting it from the tree too. The same pass removed the placement's now-inert `tolerates` entry: an exemption that covers no difference keeps silencing that literal class for the plan, so the gate now reports a reviewed tolerance nothing needs. scripts/selftest_214_hunk_gate.py grows to 15 rows and learns `@pins`, a mutation of a copy of migration/manual-pins.json, for the two gates that read the reviewed placement: the spill taken back out, and a tolerance invented for nothing. A fifth device crash was the verifier again, on a class no hand placement had ever touched: `VerifyError ... register v31 has type Reference: android.content.Context but expected Reference: qe2` in `Lv86;->e(Ljava/lang/Object;Ljava/lang/Object;)Ljava/lang/Object;` - `v86` being 194's `sv5`, whose body came over through whole-method alignment. That alignment grafted two identical 5-line runs that call `Lcom/box/app/cfg/CfgNav;->wrap`; a `/range` call needs a contiguous span, so each run copies its arguments into v14/v15/v16 and the copy clobbers all three, not just the result slot. 194 could reuse v16 there because in that frame it is not read again before it is rewritten; 214 reads it again 29 instructions later (`move-object/from16 v31, v16`) to fill the `Lqe2;` slot of `Lb96;-><init>`, and ART rejected the class - `apktool b` was silent, since v16 is a legal register and `.locals 52` still covers it. Which numbers a grafted block may clobber is a fact about the frame it was written in rather than about the call, and this block has no merge point to consult, so gates 8 and 9 could not see it. scripts/port_214_candidate.py now re-anchors a colliding staging span to the highest contiguous span of registers the method never reads again (v49/v50/v51 in `v86`) and refuses to guess when the frame has nothing dead left, reporting `no dead span` for a human placement instead; the block keeps its shape, so the only file that differs from the previous candidate is smali/v86.smali, 4 lines, same length, and migration/port-report.json records the decision under graftScratch. Liveness for both sides of it - the porter picking registers, the gate judging them - lives in one reviewed module, scripts/smali_liveness.py, which follows the method's own successors and catch entries rather than the text below, because a branch can step over a read and a write on every path that reaches it frees the register. The gate gained a tenth check, check_grafted_staging, that diffs every grafted run (reviewed placements and alignment additions alike) against the 214 upstream and reports a staged register the release still needs; it is the same rule on both sides of the hop: 0 findings on the 194 custom tree, which ships with that identical block, 1 on the broken candidate, 0 on the fixed one. scripts/selftest_214_hunk_gate.py grows to 16 rows, the new one putting v86's staging span back on v14/v15/v16. A sixth device crash came from the customization's own copied files rather than from a ported method: `AbstractMethodError: abstract method "java.lang.Object ai2.e(java.lang.Object, java.lang.Object)" on receiver java.lang.Class<com.box.app.cfg.CfgNav>`. `Lcom/box/app/cfg/CfgNav;` declares the release's two-argument composable-lambda interface - 194 spells its member `Lja2;->invoke(Ljava/lang/Object;Ljava/lang/Object;)Ljava/lang/Object;`, 214's image is `Lai2;->e(...)` - and the copy step translated everything a map can reach: the `.implements` line, the field type, and the `invoke-interface` this class makes on the delegate it wraps (now `Lai2;->e`). A method *definition* names no owner, so no map reaches it, and the tree ended up declaring `Lai2;` while defining `invoke`; `wrap` handed that object to 214 as its `Lai2;`, 214 dispatched `ai2.e`, and ART threw at run time. This gap is invisible on the way in by design: ART does not require a concrete class to implement the interfaces it declares, so `apktool b` assembles it, `check_smali_references` resolves it (the class really does define an `invoke`, nothing in the tree calls it), and the type walk has nothing to say about a method no one in the file invokes. Nine definitions across seven custom classes were orphaned the same way - `CfgNav` and `CfgIcon` `invoke` to `e`, `CfgClick`, `PanelToggle` and `RestoreCfg` `invoke` to `a`, `BattToggle` and `RestoreCfg` `invoke` to `f`, and `BootDone`'s coroutine pair `getContext`/`resumeWith` to `g`/`j` because 214 renamed `Lxd1;` as well - and the device had simply reached the first. scripts/port_214_candidate.py now realigns those definitions after the placements and the fixups, and only on the proof the member map supplies: the 194 class must declare the interface the old member belongs to, exactly one definition in the file may carry that old name with the prototype the new interface asks for, and the new name must not already be taken; anything else is reported as an `IMPL` error instead of guessed, because inventing a method name here is how a green build becomes a device crash. The nine renames are recorded in migration/port-report.json under interfaceMemberRenames, and they touch nothing but `.method` header lines in seven files. The rule behind them is one function, `unimplemented_interface_members`, which the gate re-runs as its eleventh check, `check_custom_interface_implementations`: no class this hop copies in may fail to answer an abstract member of an interface it declares. The scope is coverage's own `added` list (1356 smali files - `com/box/app` and the shipped `top/yukonga/mishka` and kotlin runtime alike) rather than a namespace prefix, because a prefix would leave 638 of those files unexamined, and because the same question asked of the whole 214 upstream returns 42 classes whose interface methods R8 deleted behind provably dead dispatch, which is legal in a compiled tree and cannot be an excuse in a copied one - and the control is the 194 customized tree, which reports nothing for the identical rule and shipped working: 9 findings on the broken candidate, 0 on the fixed one, `custom interfaces: 0/0` on the summary line. scripts/selftest_214_hunk_gate.py grows to 17 rows, the new one spelling CfgNav's definition back to 194's `invoke`. A seventh device failure arrived once the app could start a VPN at all, and it was not a Java
exception: the core itself refused to boot. `com.box.app.vpn.VpnTags` is the class that rewrites a config's
`PROCESS-NAME` clauses into per-app `SRC-IP-CIDR` tag rules for a rootless VPN, and two instructions of its
hand-written smali disagreed with the Java they were generated from. `expr()` guarded its list separator with
`if-nez v2, :cond_sep` where the source says `if (i > 0)`, so the comma landed before the first element and the
core read `OR,(,(SRC-IP-CIDR,172.19.200.1/32),…)` as a payload list whose first rule is empty: `Parse config
error: rules[5] … error: payloadRule error`, fatal, before any tunnel existed. `ip6()` wrote
`or-int/lit16 p0, p0, 0xc800`, and a 2-int/lit16 literal is signed, so tag 1 became `fdfe:dcba:9876::ffffc801`
while `VpnPump.forward6` tags the packet bytes with `0xC8,tag` - `::c801` - which is a silent permanent miss for
every IPv6 rule instead of an error. Neither could be fixed by a map: the file is *copied*, and the 171 payload
that carries it is hash-pinned history. The reviewed hop can still realign it, so `manual-pins.json` grew two
`scopedFixups` for that one file (each must fire exactly once, which the porter already enforces), the same two
lines were corrected in `decompiled/` so the runtime project, the host test and the candidate agree, and D8's own
shape for the Java expression was copied rather than invented - `VpnPump.smali` has `const v6, 0xc800` for
exactly `0xC800 | tag`. The twelfth gate, `check_copied_emitters`, walks the 1356 copied smali files for those
two traps (a `and/or/xor-int/lit16` whose literal reads as signed, and a list separator not skipped on the first
turn of an index that starts at 0 - only in methods that open a `TYPE,(` list, which is what a core config string
is made of). It is an invariant of our own files rather than a diff, because the 194 tree it came from reports
one of each: the gate exists so that the shipped tree cannot. Findings: 2 on the previous candidate, 0 now,
`emitter methods: 1` on the summary line; self-test rows 17 and 18 undo each fix in `VpnTags.smali` and must turn
the gate red (19 rows). The behavioral half of the guard lives where the artifact can be executed:
`vpn-src/test/VpnTagsTest.java` assembles the shipped `VpnTags*.smali` with the three core rewriters, enjarifies
the dex, and judges the emitted rule text - no empty element at any depth, the v6 tag equal to the pump's byte
pattern, the fallback for an uninstalled app - and `run-config-rewriters.sh` now also takes
`BOXPROXY_TEST_PROJECT` over that file. A device defect in a file nothing ports is still a device defect.
